# Proof-kit contract digest

Every contract in the kit's reference galleries, extracted from the rendered pages with the
presentation dropped. Prose is **as authored** — nothing here is summarised or rewritten.

Load in tiers — the split follows the sources' own division of labour, one file per question:

- **this file** — *which block, and am I allowed to use it.* The contract set.
- **`KIT_DIGEST_RECIPES.md`** — *how do I compose a whole page.* The 6 sanctioned recipes.
- **`KIT_DIGEST_MARKUP.md`** — *what do I paste.* The verbatim markup, load only when emitting.

## 04 · the contracts — 25 creative patterns

*Six families. The wrapper class is not optional.*

### Giant-number hero
`.fam-hero .giant` · live · 16 uses · 16 pages

- **requires** — Exactly **one** line carrying `value` + `unit` where that one figure **is** the finding, plus 2–4 further lines carrying `value` for the micro row. Rendered form: one number set ≥3× the size of any other number in the block, followed by a row of 2–4 number/label pairs.  `[machine-checkable: AF-HERO]`
- **unlocks** — Add `compare` to the headline line and the micro row can carry **movement** rather than level. Recolour the figure to `--defect` when the number is bad news — but then the legend becomes mandatory, because the hue now encodes a fact.
- **excludes** — **A number that is one of several equals.** If two figures compete for the hero slot, neither is the finding — that is a stat-strip. Also excludes **a ratio whose denominator is unstated**: a giant `94%` with no `of` is the most common dishonest block in the corpus, because the form asserts a significance the payload cannot support.
- **degrades to** — `bignum` block (same figure, no micro row) → a sentence with the number in it.

### Thesis pull-quote opener
`.fam-hero .thesis-hero` · unused · 0 uses

- **requires** — One **declarative sentence** ≤ ~140 characters that is itself the finding, plus a verdict word from a closed set, plus a dated as-of. **No number required** — this is the pattern for a finding that has none, which is why the corpus's number-shaped payloads never reach it.  `[human-only]`
- **unlocks** — The drop-cap; `<em>` on the load-bearing phrase; the chip swapping to CONFIRMED / REFUTED once a verdict exists.
- **excludes** — **A summary of several findings.** If the sentence contains an “and” joining two independent claims, it is a claim-ledger wearing a serif. Also excludes anything hedged: a claim you cannot attach a verdict chip to has no business at 44px, and setting it there is an emphasis you have not earned.
- **degrades to** — `thesis` block → a lede paragraph.

### Verdict hero card
`.fam-hero .vcard` · unused · 0 uses

- **requires** — **1–3 gates**, each carrying all three of: a categorical verdict from the closed set `pass | fail | proven`, one metric with a unit, and a one-line ruling. Rendered form: ≥1 element carrying a verdict word with an adjacent number in the same card.  `[machine-checkable: AF-VERDICT]`
- **unlocks** — A row of three compares gates side by side at a glance. The colour legend becomes **mandatory**, not optional — the band hue is the verdict.
- **excludes** — **A verdict with no metric.** A naked PASS card is a chip that has been inflated to hero size; the reader cannot audit it. And never more than three — four or more gates is a `verdict-dashboard` or a claim-ledger, and cramming them here turns a ruling into wallpaper.
- **degrades to** — `claim-verdict` row → `callout --insight` carrying the ruling.

### Split hero
`.fam-hero .split` · unused · 0 uses

- **requires** — One claim sentence **and** exactly one supporting visual that is a genuinely **different channel** from the sentence: a spark series (≥5 points), a single stat, or a 3–5 row dot cluster. Two things, two channels, one row.  `[structural only: structure yes, “different channel” no]`
- **unlocks** — The right rail takes any one of the three blocks; the sparkline specifically needs a **series**, so having `at`-stamped history upgrades a stat into a spark.
- **excludes** — **A claim paired with a restatement of itself.** If the right-hand stat is the grammatical subject of the left-hand sentence, you have a giant-number hero with extra words — the split promises two independent readings and delivers one.
- **degrades to** — `thesis` + a separate `bignum`, stacked → `thesis` alone.

### Diagonal split
`.fam-comparison .diag` · unused · 0 uses

- **requires** — Exactly **two states of one subject**, each with a headline figure, plus **one** signed delta between them, plus 2–4 short supporting rows per side. The badge at the seam is singular by construction.  `[machine-checkable: AF-DELTA (1 pair)]`
- **unlocks** — The seam delta badge; per-side `.rows` marks for the supporting detail.
- **excludes** — **More than one metric moving.** The diagonal has exactly one badge, so a second delta has nowhere honest to go and gets demoted to a supporting row — an emphasis lie. Use the delta gutter. Also excludes A-vs-B of two **different subjects**: the diagonal seam asserts a transformation of one thing over time, not a comparison of two things.
- **degrades to** — `.sbs` delta gutter → `table --delta`.

### Overlay diff
`.fam-comparison .odiff` · unused · 0 uses

- **requires** — A before/after pair differing by a **token-level substring**: the removed token and its replacement must both be quotable inline, inside one line of ≤ ~80 characters. Rendered form: a `.was` and a `.now` adjacent in the same text node.  `[machine-checkable: AF-DELTA (token)]`
- **unlocks** — The serif `.quotable` lift — the change restated as a sentence a reader can carry away without the code.
- **excludes** — **A multi-line change** — that is the `diff` block, and inlining it produces an unreadable ribbon. Also excludes a change where the removed token is **empty**: a pure addition rendered as an overlay reads as noise, because the strike-through channel has nothing to carry.
- **degrades to** — `diff` block → `code` block with the line marked.

### Side-by-side + delta gutter
`.fam-comparison .sbs` · live · 20 uses · 17 pages

- **requires** — N ≥ 2 metrics, each with a before value, an after value, and **the same unit on both sides**; plus a direction judgment per row (better / worse) that is **stated by the author**, not inferred from the sign.  `[machine-checkable: AF-DELTA (N pairs)]`
- **unlocks** — The `.gcol.better` / `.worse` tint + arrow; a summary row once the column is summable.
- **excludes** — **Mixed polarity under one colour rule.** If “higher is better” is true for some rows and false for others, a single green-up convention is dishonest — and this is the most common misuse of the most-used comparison pattern in the corpus. State direction per row or split the block. Also excludes a single row: one pair is a was→now strip.
- **degrades to** — `table --delta` (signed direction column) → a plain two-column table.

### Was → now strip
`.fam-comparison .strip` · unused · 0 uses

- **requires** — A, B, **and the named transform between them** — the mechanism, as a short mono label. Two of three is not this pattern: without the mechanism, the middle column is decoration.  `[structural only: three columns yes, “named” no]`
- **unlocks** — The arrow + mono pill; vertical restack with a rotated arrow at narrow widths, so it survives 390px without an `overflow` escape.
- **excludes** — **A before/after whose transform you cannot name** — “we fixed it” is not a mechanism. The whole pattern is a **causal** claim: A became B *by* this operation. If you can only assert correlation, use a delta gutter, which claims nothing about why.
- **degrades to** — `.sbs` delta gutter with one row → `diff`.

### Confidence band
`.fam-dataviz (svg)` · unreachable-today · **UNREACHABLE TODAY**

- **requires** — One line carrying `value` **and** `range` {lo, hi} **and** a stated threshold on the same scale, plus the scale's domain. All four, or the shaded interval means nothing a reader can act on.  `[machine-checkable: AF-INTERVAL]`
- **blocked-by** — **Measured, not assumed:** `range` appears in 5 of 57 documents, and none of those five pairs it with a threshold. The pattern is not merely unused — the payload that would fill it is produced roughly nowhere, and half-filling it (an interval with no threshold) produces a chart whose only reading is “there is uncertainty”.
- **excludes** — **An interval you did not compute.** Rendering ±10% because it “looks about right” is fabrication with a confidence interval's authority. Also excludes a metric where higher-is-better is ambiguous — the band's gradient direction encodes a claim about which end is good.
- **degrades to** — `bignum` with the interval in the sub-line (“96.8% ± 1.2”) → a sentence stating value, interval and threshold.

### Coverage heatmap
`.fam-dataviz (svg)` · unused · n/a — no per-pattern class

- **requires** — A **rows × columns matrix** with **one comparable value per cell** on a single scale — i.e. lines carrying `group` of depth 2 plus a `value`. Rendered form: a table with ≥3 rows × ≥2 numeric columns and a row-header column.  `[machine-checkable: AF-MATRIX]`
- **unlocks** — The cold-column read — the eye finds the worst column before it reads a single label, which is the one thing a table cannot do. Modulate opacity for magnitude on top of a scale-token hue.
- **excludes** — **Cells on different scales.** A grid mixing percentages, counts and durations is a table with a tint applied; the shared colour ramp asserts comparability that does not exist. Also excludes a sparse matrix — if most cells are empty the pattern reads as a coverage claim you have not made.
- **degrades to** — `table` with the numbers printed (which is why the numbers must be printed in the heatmap too) → per-row `meter`.

### Distribution / histogram
`.fam-dataviz (svg)` · unused · n/a — no per-pattern class

- **requires** — Many lines binned on **one continuous numeric**, with the bin width stated, plus a marked median. Below roughly 20 observations the bins are noise wearing a chart.  `[structural only: bars yes, “continuous” no]`
- **unlocks** — The shape reading — a skewed tail the mean would have hidden. This is the only pattern in the kit whose payoff is a **disagreement with a summary statistic**.
- **excludes** — **Categorical bars.** A bar per named thing is a ranking — use bars-in-table, where the labels get room and the order is meaningful. A histogram's x-axis must be ordered *by magnitude of the binned variable*; if reordering the bars is legal, it is not a distribution. Also: the median line must be **solid** — dashed is reserved.
- **degrades to** — `stat-strip` carrying median + p95 + max (the three numbers the shape was for) → a sentence naming the skew.

### Bars-in-table
`.fam-dataviz (svg in a table)` · unused · n/a — no per-pattern class

- **requires** — A **ranked** list: N lines with one `value` on a shared scale and a `group` of depth 1, sorted. The bar is scaled to `value / max`, so a max must exist and be stated.  `[machine-checkable: AF-SHARES]`
- **unlocks** — Both readings at once — exact figure *and* relative magnitude — which is the one thing a bare table and a bare bar chart each give up. Add `of` and the same row becomes a `meter`.
- **excludes** — **Dropping the number column.** Without it this is a bar chart wearing table chrome, and the exactness the table form promises is not delivered. Also excludes unsorted rows: an unsorted bar column invites a length comparison the reading order actively fights.
- **degrades to** — `table` sorted descending → `table` unsorted.

### Gauge / meter row
`.fam-dataviz (svg)` · unused · n/a — no per-pattern class

- **requires** — 2–4 KPIs, each with a `value`, a **scale maximum**, and **its own target**. The target is what distinguishes a gauge from a decorated percentage: the arc colour is a comparison, not a level.  `[machine-checkable: AF-SHARES + threshold]`
- **unlocks** — Pass / close / fail colouring by comparing value to target, plus a threshold tick at the target angle — the reader gets the verdict without arithmetic.
- **excludes** — **A KPI with no target.** A gauge without a tick is a pie chart of one number, and the dial form implies a “should be here” that you have not stated. Also excludes more than four — a gauge row is a header strip, and five dials is a dashboard nobody reads.
- **degrades to** — `meter` block (bars, shares of a whole) → `stat-strip` with the target in each label.

### Callout-pins overlay
`.fam-annotated .keyed / .pin` · unreachable-today · ~~**UNREACHABLE TODAY**~~ **→ REACHABLE, UNEXERCISED (blocker falsified 2026-08-02)**

- **requires** — One **captured** exhibit + **N ≥ 2 region coordinates** as x/y percentages, each paired 1:1 with a sentence. The pairing is the pattern: a pin without a note and a note without a pin are both defects.  `[machine-checkable: pin/li count parity]`
- **blocked-by** — ~~No image files and no coordinates exist in the corpus. Measured, not assumed.~~ **FALSIFIED 2026-08-02, both halves** (`aperture_LOG.md:60`): image files are abundant (see the `figure` row) **and** region coordinates exist as committed data (`specrail-geometry.json`). Reach for this pattern; it is unexercised, not blocked.
- **excludes** — An exhibit you authored (see above). Also excludes **one** pin — a single annotation is a caption, and the numbered-key apparatus costs the reader more than it returns. And excludes pins on regions a reader cannot verify: if the pin points at something the exhibit does not actually show, the number lends borrowed credibility to a claim.
- **degrades to** — `figure` + an ordered list beneath it (same content, no spatial binding) → `figure` with a prose caption.

### Leader-line margin annotations
`.fam-annotated .mnote` · unreachable-today · ~~**UNREACHABLE TODAY**~~ **→ REACHABLE, UNEXERCISED (blocker falsified 2026-08-02)**

- **requires** — A **tall** captured exhibit + N annotation targets whose leader lines are authored **in the exhibit's own viewBox units**, never in page pixels. Notes need vertical room, so the exhibit must be taller than it is wide or the margin has nowhere to go.  `[structural only: viewBox units yes, “tall” yes, the rest no]`
- **blocked-by** — ~~Same blocker: no captured exhibits. Measured, not assumed.~~ **FALSIFIED 2026-08-02** (`aperture_LOG.md:60`): captured exhibits are abundant — `ex-ledger-dark-390.png` (537×3443) is exactly the tall exhibit this pattern asks for. Reach for it; it is unexercised, not blocked.
- **excludes** — **Leader lines drawn outside the exhibit's coordinate system.** A line positioned in page pixels desyncs from the image the first time the layout reflows or the viewport changes — and it desyncs *silently*, still pointing confidently at the wrong thing. This is a correctness constraint, not a styling one. Also excludes a wide exhibit, where the margin collapses at 390px and every leader crosses every other.
- **degrades to** — Callout-pins (numbered, no lines — nothing to desync) → `figure` + list.

### Highlighted crop + zoom
`.fam-annotated .cropwrap / .roilegend` · unreachable-today · ~~**UNREACHABLE TODAY**~~ **→ REACHABLE, UNEXERCISED (blocker falsified 2026-08-02)**

- **requires** — A captured exhibit + **one** region of interest + a magnified view of **the same pixels**, obtained by windowing the same source (a tighter `data:` URI or a cropped viewBox). Plus the magnification factor, stated.  `[structural only: two views yes, “same pixels” no]`
- **blocked-by** — ~~Same blocker: no captured exhibits. Measured, not assumed.~~ **FALSIFIED 2026-08-02** (`aperture_LOG.md:60`): captured exhibits are abundant. Reach for it; it is unexercised, not blocked.
- **excludes** — **A redrawn detail.** If the zoom is re-rendered rather than windowed, it is an illustration of the claim, not the evidence for it — and it will be cleaner than the original in exactly the way that hides the defect you are pointing at. Also excludes multiple ROIs: two crops is the callout-pins pattern, and the crop form implies “this one place is where the proof lives”.
- **degrades to** — `figure` of the full render with the ROI described in the caption → `quote` of the small print itself.

### Spec-rail annotated exhibit
`.fam-annotated .specrail` · unreachable-today · ~~**UNREACHABLE TODAY**~~ **→ REACHABLE, UNEXERCISED (blocker falsified 2026-08-02 — the most falsified of the six)**

- **requires** — An exhibit that **is itself a measurement** (a bounding-box overlay, a layout extraction, a diff render) + A/B/C anchor marks dropped at the **measured** points + a mono rail giving each mark's real value and its own provenance tag. The numbers are the proof; the picture is the index into them.  `[machine-checkable: mark/rail-row parity]`
- **blocked-by** — ~~No measurement renders and no coordinates in the corpus. **This is the one annotated pattern a hand-authored SVG could legitimately satisfy** — plotted from real extracted geometry, the drawing *is* the data — but the geometry does not exist either. Measured, not assumed.~~ **FALSIFIED 2026-08-02** (`aperture_LOG.md:60`) — and it is the most falsified of the six, because **the blocker nominated its own satisfier and that satisfier now exists**: `specrail-geometry.json` carries per-region `left`/`width` in the exhibit's own coordinate space, bound by name to `ex-specrail-dark-390.png`, with the device scalar stated; `capture-specrail.mjs:1` captures the pixels and the numbers in one run *"so the pixels and the numbers are the same render."* Reach for it; it is unexercised, not blocked.
- **excludes** — **Marks placed by eye.** The entire authority of this pattern is that mark A sits where the measurement says it sits; nudging it for composition converts a measurement render into an illustration while keeping its typography. Also excludes a uniform provenance rail — if every row is checked-here, drop the column rather than render a constant.
- **degrades to** — `table` of the measured values (the rail alone, which carries the whole proof) → `code` block of the raw extraction.

### Vertical timeline (recency spine)
`.fam-narrative .tl-node` · live · 89 uses · 19 pages

- **requires** — N ≥ 3 lines each carrying `at` — a **real, parseable, verifiable** date — in order, plus the page's as-of so each node can be bucketed for recency. Rendered form: ≥3 ISO dates in one block, monotonic.  `[structural only: AF-SEQUENCE sees dates, not their truth]`
- **unlocks** — Recency dots (needs as-of, and the `legend --freshness` block becomes mandatory the moment they appear). Add a boolean per node and milestones punctuate the run.
- **excludes** — **A sequence with no real dates.** Steps numbered 1…N are a step-flow; reaching the timeline by inventing plausible dates is the specific failure this clause exists to prevent, because the recency dots then encode a fabrication in the kit's most trusted colour channel. Also excludes ~15+ nodes with no milestones — an unpunctuated spine is a list that has bought a graphic.
- **degrades to** — `sequence --timeline` block (dates, no recency) → `sequence --numbered` → an ordered list.

### Step-flow with state
`.fam-narrative .step` · unused · 0 uses

- **requires** — N ≥ 3 ordered steps, each with a title and a `state` from the **closed set** `done | failed | running | pending`. Rendered form: ≥3 items each carrying a lifecycle word.  `[machine-checkable: AF-STATES]`
- **unlocks** — The state pill + its paired glyph (colour is never alone here — the glyph carries it). Add a real command per step and `.step-cmd` turns the ledger into a reproduction script.
- **excludes** — **Steps that are all in the same state.** An all-`done` step-flow carries nothing the numbered list did not, and the state column becomes a constant that reads as information. Use `sequence --numbered`. Also excludes inventing a fifth state: the legend's set is closed, and a novel word is a swatch the reader has no key for.
- **degrades to** — `sequence --numbered` (repro steps) → an ordered list.

### Story arc (three beats)
`.fam-narrative .beat` · unused · 0 uses

- **requires** — Exactly **three** beats — setup, turn, resolve — where the turn is **a stated contradiction**: what was expected, and what was actually found instead. The reversal is the precondition; three-ness is only its consequence.  `[human-only]`
- **unlocks** — The turn takes `--defect` and the resolve `--seal` (via `.beat.turn` / `.beat.resolve`) — so the colour tracks the argument, not the ordinal. One pull-line per beat, prose held at reading measure.
- **excludes** — **A three-part story with no surprise.** If beat 2 is “then we did the next thing”, this is a timeline with literary pretensions — and the `--defect` tint on the turn then flags a defect that does not exist. The arc is earned by a contradiction, never by a count of three.
- **degrades to** — Vertical timeline with three nodes → three paragraphs under a `thesis`.

### Horizontal phase pipeline
`.fam-narrative .phase` · unused · 0 uses

- **requires** — N named phases in a **fixed** left-to-right order, **exactly one** marked `active`, every other in `done | blocked | upcoming`; and for any `blocked` phase, **the blocker named**.  `[machine-checkable: AF-PIPELINE-ACTIVE]`
- **unlocks** — The where-are-we-and-what-is-stuck read at a glance. Add `at` per phase and `.phase-when` dates the march.
- **excludes** — **Zero actives, and two actives.** The pattern's whole job is answering “where are we”; no answer makes it a checklist, and two answers is not an answer. This is also the cleanest structural defect on the sheet — a checker can count `.phase.active` and be certain. Also excludes a process whose order is not fixed: if phases can run out of order, that is a step-flow.
- **degrades to** — `pipeline --phases` block → `pipeline --flow` → a labelled list with the current item marked.

### Claim-ledger
`.fam-provenance .lg-ev` · live · 96 uses · 16 pages

- **requires** — **3–8 discrete claims**, each carrying all three of: ≥1 evidence item with a ref, a verdict from a closed set (`Proven | Partial | Refuted`), and a provenance tag (`checked-here | trusted-upstream`). Rendered form: ≥3 claim+verdict pairs in one block.  `[machine-checkable: AF-LEDGER]`
- **unlocks** — The verdict vocabulary is swappable; the provenance column is not. A sealed footer becomes available only when every row is Proven — and it is a real claim, so do not render it otherwise.
- **excludes** — **Claims you cannot attach a verdict to.** An open question parked in a ledger row reads as Refuted to anyone scanning the verdict column — the register form forces a ruling onto material that has none. Park them in a `qa` block instead. Also excludes fewer than three (a register of two is a callout) and more than eight (past that the eye stops reading rows and starts reading the verdict column, which is a `verdict-dashboard`).
- **degrades to** — `claim-verdict` rows (same content, no register frame) → `table --status`.

### Evidence-stack
`.fam-provenance .srccard` · live · 80 uses · 16 pages

- **requires** — **One** claim + **2–4 sources of genuinely different kinds** — e.g. a document, a log line, a query result — each naming its kind and its ref. Rendered form: `.sc-kind` values within one stack must not all be identical.  `[machine-checkable: AF-STACK-MONOKIND]`
- **unlocks** — The convergence line — “over-determined by N kinds”. The offset and shadow are the only place in the family where depth is spent, and they are what makes the stack read as layered rather than listed.
- **excludes** — **Two-to-four sources of the same kind.** Three greps of one file are one source seen three times; stacking them asserts a convergence that does not exist, and does it in the family whose entire job is honest origin. This is the pattern's honesty condition, not a preference — and unusually, it is **mechanically checkable**: identical `.sc-kind` values across a stack is a structural defect a rule can find.
- **degrades to** — `claim-verdict` with a multi-item proof cell → a `callout` listing the refs.

### Receipt / manifest
`.fam-provenance .rc-line` · unused · 0 uses

- **requires** — **≥5 itemized lines**, each with a label, a count, a status glyph and a here/up tag; **plus a stated total**; **plus an arithmetic relation the reader can verify** — the lines sum to the total. Rendered form: ≥5 labelled counts in one block.  `[machine-checkable: AF-MANIFEST + sum check]`
- **unlocks** — The verdict footer, and the best property in the family: **a failing checksum is itself the finding** — the form that proves completeness also proves incompleteness, at no extra cost.
- **excludes** — **A list of items with no arithmetic.** If the lines do not sum to anything, the receipt form promises a completeness claim you are not making — and it promises it in mono, centred, with a checksum, which is about as much borrowed authority as the kit can lend. Never fabricate the digest: an unverifiable checksum is worse than none, because it is specifically designed to look verified.
- **degrades to** — `table --total` (the arithmetic, no ceremony) → a bulleted list of what was checked.

### Provenance ribbon
`.fam-provenance .ribbon-legend` · unused · 0 uses

- **requires** — Flowing prose in which provenance is **genuinely mixed at sentence granularity** — ≥2 assertions checked-here and ≥1 trusted-upstream, or the reverse. Each assertion needs its own ref.  `[machine-checkable: ≥2 distinct .rb-assert classes]`
- **unlocks** — The reserved channel, used exactly as intended: solid accent spine = checked-here, hatched spine = trusted-upstream. This is the only pattern in the kit whose whole vocabulary *is* the dashed/solid distinction, which is why nothing else may spend it.
- **excludes** — **Uniform provenance.** A ribbon where every spine is solid is decoration wearing an honesty signal — put one `prov` word in the `.mod-foot` and be done. This is the pattern the honest-presentation rule most invites and least needs: reaching for it because provenance *feels* important, when there is only one kind of it, is how the reserved channel gets devalued.
- **degrades to** — An inline `.prov` chip per assertion → a single `prov` value in the block's `.mod-foot`.

## 05 · the contracts — 20 static blocks

*The layer everything above degrades into. It has to hold.*

### stat-strip
`.stripe --tiled` · live · 3 uses · 2 pages

- **requires** — **3–5 lines with `value`**, of comparable weight and the same kind of figure — headline numbers that share a frame of reference.  `[structural only: cell count yes, “same kind” no]`
- **unlocks** — `--tiled` adds a per-cell state dot and footnote — available once each figure carries its own state, and it drags the `legend` block in with it.
- **excludes** — **Figures with different denominators presented as equals.** Equal-weight cells assert comparability; three percentages of three different populations is a strip that lies by alignment alone. Also excludes a single figure — that is `bignum`.
- **degrades to** — `table` with a label and value column.

### bignum
`.bignum --spark` · live · 21 uses · 17 pages

- **requires** — **Exactly one** `value` + `unit`, plus a one-line statement of what it means, plus **the basis it was computed over** (n, window, or source).  `[structural only: AF-HERO finds the figure, not the basis]`
- **unlocks** — `--spark` once a series of ≥5 points sits behind the number — the level plus its trajectory, at no extra vertical cost.
- **excludes** — **A number with no stated basis.** The block's whole rhetorical move is “this figure is the finding”; without n, window or source the reader cannot tell a measurement from an impression, and the type size makes the difference feel settled.
- **degrades to** — A sentence containing the number and its basis.

### table
`.tablewrap --delta --status --total` · live · 20 uses · 17 pages

- **requires** — ≥2 rows × ≥2 columns, each column holding **one consistent type**. That consistency is the contract — it is what makes a column comparable down its length.  `[machine-checkable: table geometry]`
- **unlocks** — `--delta` once each row has a before and an after · `--status` once verdicts come from a closed set · `--total` once a column is genuinely summable. Add a shared scale across columns and a **coverage heatmap** becomes available.
- **excludes** — A single row (a table of one is a definition list wearing a grid) and **prose paragraphs in cells** — a cell the eye has to read rather than scan defeats the only advantage the form has. Also excludes `--total` on a column of percentages or ratios.
- **degrades to** — A definition list → a bulleted list.

### meter
`.meters .meter` · live · 17 uses · 4 pages

- **requires** — ≥2 lines with `value` **and** `of`, where `of` is **the same whole** for every line. Shares, not levels.  `[machine-checkable: AF-SHARES]`
- **unlocks** — The dual read — percentage *and* absolute count in one row (`64% · 1,478`), which is what stops a share from hiding a small n.
- **excludes** — **Shares that do not share a denominator**, and any set summing past 100%. The bar length is a claim about a common whole; break that and the bars are comparing nothing. If the parts genuinely overlap, use `table` and say so.
- **degrades to** — `table` with a percent column and the denominator in the caption.

### sequence
`.tl-item / .proclist / .clog` · live · 3 uses · 2 pages

- **requires** — ≥3 items where **the order carries meaning** — reordering them changes what the block says.  `[structural only: ≥3 ordered items yes, “meaningful” no]`
- **unlocks** — `--timeline` once every item has `at` · `--numbered` for repro steps · `--log` once each item carries a type from `add | fix | chg`. With `at` present, the **vertical timeline** pattern also comes into range.
- **excludes** — An unordered set. If the items can be shuffled without loss, the numbering is decoration that implies a dependency chain the data does not have.
- **degrades to** — A `<ul>`.

### pipeline
`.flow .phases --flow --phases` · live · 1 use · 1 page

- **requires** — ≥3 **named** stages in fixed left-to-right order, with a stated relation between them (output of one feeds the next).  `[structural only: ≥3 named stages yes, “feeds the next” no]`
- **unlocks** — `--flow` draws the connectors · `--phases` once each stage carries a state, which also brings the **phase pipeline** pattern into range.
- **excludes** — A branching process — the left-to-right line asserts a single path, so a fork rendered here silently drops an arm. Use `branch`. Also excludes unnamed stages: “Step 2” is a count, not a stage.
- **degrades to** — `sequence` → a labelled list.

### branch
`.branch` · loose only · 0 strict · 3 loose

- **requires** — One question with a **decidable** condition, and ≥2 **mutually exclusive** arms, each with its own consequence. Exclusivity is the precondition, not the styling.  `[human-only]`
- **unlocks** — Yes/no arm styling once the condition is genuinely binary.
- **excludes** — A progression dressed as a fork (use `sequence`), and more than three arms — past that the fork geometry stops helping and a condition→outcome `table` reads faster. Also excludes arms that can both fire: the form asserts exclusivity, and a reader will act on that.
- **degrades to** — `table` of condition → outcome.

### claim-verdict
`.cpv` · live · 1 use · 1 page

- **requires** — Per row: a claim, **a proof that is not the claim restated**, and a verdict. All three cells populated — the row is the unit.  `[structural only: cells non-empty yes, “not restated” no]`
- **unlocks** — Three or more rows with provenance tags brings the **claim-ledger** pattern into range — same content, register frame.
- **excludes** — **A proof cell that paraphrases the claim cell.** “Claim: no network requests. Proof: it makes no network requests.” — the three-column form promises independent corroboration, and this is the most common way the corpus's most argument-shaped block gets filled with nothing.
- **degrades to** — `callout --insight` stating the claim and its evidence in a sentence.

### thesis
`.thesis-block` · live · 34 strict · 58 loose · 42 pages

- **requires** — **The one framing premise** the rest of the page depends on — a single sentence that, if false, invalidates what follows.  `[machine-checkable: AF-THESIS-DUP (count per page)]`
- **unlocks** — `<em>` on the load-bearing phrase. Add a verdict chip and a dated as-of and the **thesis pull-quote opener** comes into range.
- **excludes** — **More than one per page.** Two theses is none — the reader cannot tell which claim the page rests on, and the second one silently demotes the first. This is trivially checkable and worth checking: the block appears on 42 pages, more than any other structural block.
- **degrades to** — A lede paragraph at reading measure.

### scope
`.scope .scope-card` · live · 19 strict · 64 loose · 43 pages

- **requires** — **All three** boundaries populated: what is **shown**, what is **out**, and what **rests upstream** (trusted, not re-derived). Three cards, none empty.  `[machine-checkable: AF-SCOPE-EMPTY]`
- **unlocks** — Nothing further — and that is the point. This block is a floor, not a platform.
- **excludes** — **An empty “out” list.** A claim of no limits is the least believable thing that can appear on a proof page, and rendering the card empty is worse than omitting the block — it shows you were asked and had nothing. The same holds for an empty “rests upstream”: on a page with any trusted-upstream figure, that card cannot honestly be blank.
- **degrades to** — A `callout --caution` naming the single biggest limit.

### qa
`.qa .qa-row` · live · 17 strict · 55 loose · 37 pages

- **requires** — ≥2 questions a **sceptical reader would actually ask**, each answered **verdict-led** — the answer's first clause is the ruling, the rest is support.  `[structural only: ≥2 rows yes, “would actually ask” no]`
- **unlocks** — The `.lead.warn` variant for an answer that concedes rather than defends — which is the block earning its keep.
- **excludes** — **Questions invented because they were easy to answer.** A qa block that never concedes anything is an advertisement with a question mark; the form's credibility comes entirely from the reader recognising their own objection. If none of your answers begins with “yes, and that is a real limit”, you wrote the wrong questions.
- **degrades to** — A `callout --caution` per genuine objection → prose.

### tradeoff
`.tradeoff` · live · 1 strict · 6 loose · 5 pages

- **requires** — A decision, and **a real cost on both sides** — each side's column non-empty and naming something you would genuinely lose.  `[structural only: both columns non-empty yes, “real cost” no]`
- **unlocks** — Nothing further. Like `scope`, this is a floor.
- **excludes** — **A “tradeoff” where one side has no cost.** That is a recommendation, and dressing it in this block is a rhetorical move: the form's symmetry implies you weighed something, and the reader extends credit accordingly. Either find the real cost of your preferred option or use `callout --insight` and recommend openly.
- **degrades to** — `callout --note` stating the recommendation and its one known cost.

### figure
`.frame` · frame-only · 0 strict · 18 loose · ~~**UNREACHABLE TODAY**~~ **→ REACHABLE (blocker falsified 2026-08-02)**

- **requires** — A **real rendered asset that exists** — a resolvable `src`, not a placeholder plate — plus a caption stating what it shows and where it came from.  `[machine-checkable: AF-FIGURE-EMPTY]`
- **blocked-by** — ~~Zero image files exist anywhere in the corpus, so every one of the 18 loose uses is a frame around a placeholder or a hand-authored SVG. **The block is styled and reachable; the assets are not produced.**~~ **BLOCKER FALSIFIED 2026-08-02** — this is the second, uncorrected copy of the claim already struck in the *Unreachable today* list above. Rendered assets are **abundant**: **9,061 `.png` + 23 `.jpg` + 24 `.webp` (6.5 GB)** across dozens of directories, produced systematically by the render discipline. The real constraint is **embedding, not absence** — a CSP-safe self-contained page carries images as `data:` URIs, so the limit is a per-page byte budget, and the kit already ships one `data:` grain URI, proving the mechanism. **Fixing this fixed five patterns at once**, exactly as the original entry predicted it would.
- **excludes** — **A placeholder shipped as evidence.** The plate is an authoring affordance, not a rendering — leaving it in a published page means the frame's implicit “here is the thing itself” is carrying a claim with nothing behind it. If the capture does not exist yet, say so in prose.
- **degrades to** — `code` block of the raw output the render would have shown → a sentence describing it and naming the ref.

### diff
`.diff .diffcol` · loose only · 0 strict · 3 loose

- **requires** — A before **and** after excerpt of **the same source**, ≤ ~12 lines each, with the file ref. Both columns, or it is a `code` block.  `[structural only: two columns yes, “same source” no]`
- **unlocks** — When the change collapses to a single token, the **overlay diff** pattern becomes available and reads far better.
- **excludes** — **A diff of output rather than source.** Two log excerpts side by side look identical to a source diff and prove something entirely different — behaviour changed, not code. Label it as output or use two `code --term` blocks.
- **degrades to** — `code` block of the after state with the change described.

### code
`.codewrap --term` · live · 3 uses · 2 pages

- **requires** — A **verbatim** excerpt plus a ref precise enough to re-fetch it (file + line, or the exact command).  `[human-only: human-only — “verbatim” is unverifiable from the page]`
- **unlocks** — `--term` gives dark terminal chrome, which is a claim in itself: *this is what the machine actually printed*.
- **excludes** — **Retyped, tidied or paraphrased code.** Monospace in a bordered well is a verbatim claim; cleaning up a stack trace to fit is the quiet version of fabricating it. If you must elide, mark the elision. `--term` in particular must never carry output you composed.
- **degrades to** — Inline `<code>` for the one identifier that matters, plus the ref.

### quote
`.cite --pull` · live · 1 use · 1 page

- **requires** — A **verbatim** line plus an attributable source — a person, a document, or a log — carried in a provenance chip.  `[human-only]`
- **unlocks** — `--pull` for a display interrupt, once the line is short enough to survive being set large.
- **excludes** — **Paraphrase inside quotation marks**, and a quote with no attributable source. The quote block's entire value is that someone else said it; an unattributed one is your own sentence wearing borrowed authority, and readers grant quotes more credit than prose precisely because they assume attribution was checked.
- **degrades to** — Prose stating the point in your own voice with a ref.

### callout
`.callout --insight --caution --note` · live · 41 strict · 536 loose · 51 pages

- **requires** — **One** point, stepping out of the body, with **a stated intent** from the closed set `insight | caution | note`. The intent is the precondition: a callout without one is a paragraph that has been indented.  `[machine-checkable: AF-CALLOUT-RATIO]`
- **unlocks** — The three intent hues, each with its own title convention. Nothing else — this block is deliberately shallow.
- **excludes** — **Use as a paragraph container.** Measured: 536 loose uses across 51 pages — an order of magnitude past every other block, and the clearest signal in the histogram that the corpus composes by reaching for the same shape twice a page. **The rule: if a page's callouts outnumber its other blocks, the callouts are prose** and should be set as prose. Emphasis that never stops is not emphasis.
- **degrades to** — A paragraph — which, for most of those 536, is the correct rendering.

### legend
`.legendbox .scale --freshness --chips` · live · 33 strict · 45 loose · 29 pages

- **requires** — **Any colour anywhere on the page that encodes a fact.** That is the whole trigger — and it makes this the only **mandatory** entry on the sheet. One row per hue, each naming the bucket in words.  `[machine-checkable: AF-LEGEND-MISSING]`
- **unlocks** — `--freshness` for the recency ramp · `--chips` for provenance and verdict vocabularies. A hue you cannot write a legend row for is a hue you have not decided the meaning of.
- **excludes** — **A legend for decorative colour** — there should not be any, and legending it grants meaning to noise. Conversely, and far more common: **shipping the hues without the key**. The freshness ramp appears on 29 pages; every page carrying it owes the reader this block.
- **degrades to** — **Nothing. This is the one block with no fallback.** If colour encodes a fact and there is no legend, the correct move is not a smaller legend — it is to **remove the colour** and carry the distinction in words.

### verdict-dashboard
`.vcell` · never used · 0 / 0

- **requires** — **≥6 claims that already carry verdicts** — that is, a claim-ledger must exist first. This block summarises a register; it does not create one.  `[machine-checkable: ≥6 .vcell + a ledger on the page]`
- **unlocks** — The whole register's state in one scan, which is exactly what a ledger stops delivering past eight rows.
- **excludes** — **Standing alone.** A dashboard without the ledger it summarises is a grid of verdicts with no evidence anywhere on the page — the form's density reads as rigour while carrying none. Also excludes fewer than six cells: below that the ledger itself already scans.
- **degrades to** — **Claim-ledger** pattern → `claim-verdict` rows.

### coverage-map
`.cov-legend` · never used · 0 / 0

- **requires** — A set of checkable units, each labelled `checked | skipped-deliberately | not-reached`, **and a reason for every skip**. Same matrix shape as the coverage heatmap, but the values are categorical rather than continuous.  `[structural only: the matrix yes, “a reason per skip” no]`
- **unlocks** — Spatial gap-finding — the eye lands on the not-reached region before reading a label. Give the cells a shared numeric scale instead and the **coverage heatmap** pattern applies.
- **excludes** — **A map with no skips.** The block exists to show the gaps; an all-green map is a completeness claim rendered as a diagram, and it is the exact shape a reader trusts most and can audit least. Also excludes skips with no reason — “not-reached” without a why is where the honest version of this block goes to die.
- **degrades to** — `table --status` with a reason column → `scope` naming what was out.

## Opener hero forms — 5

A different contract dialect from the sheet above: the second clause is **Composes**, not
**unlocks**, and there is no status/checkability channel. Source page: `openers.html` §4.

### OP-H1 · giant-number hero
- **requires** — Exactly one line with `value`+`unit` that *is* the finding, with **no other line outranking it** (`LINE_ENTITY_DESIGN` §3: *1 line, value+unit, no group*), **plus 2–4 supporting lines** carrying `value`. The scalar must be one a reader has a reference for — a rate, a count of things they can picture, a share. An id, a byte total, or a duration nobody has a baseline for is a number, not a finding.
- **composes** — In this order: eyebrow **R3** → figure **R1** → meaning line **R2** (one sentence; states what the number *means* and never repeats it) → stat strip **R2** → apparatus **R4**. The title **demotes to R2** (`.op-title.r2`) or is dropped — the number is the title. A verdict **chip** may ride the eyebrow at R3.
- **excludes** — **A verdict stamp** — two R1s (fight F1). **A dek** — the meaning line already is one (matrix ✕). **Any stat cell repeating the hero figure. An undemoted title. `--shadow-card` / `--shadow-deep`** — an opener is paper (fight F6).
- **degrades to** — Fewer than 2 supporting stats → **stat-strip opener**: all figures at equal weight, none enlarged. Zero supporting stats → **OP-H5 quiet**, with the number bolded inline in the dek. Never inflate a lone number to 100px — with nothing beside it, it reads as a slide, not as a finding.
- *copyable markup:* `KIT_DIGEST_MARKUP.md` → "OP-H1 · giant-number hero"

### OP-H2 · verdict hero
- **requires** — A categorical ruling over a **named gate with a stated threshold**, and a number on the page that visibly clears or breaches it — the verdict must be **recomputable by the reader** from what the opener shows. A verdict with no threshold is an opinion in a box. It also requires an **on-page legend**, because the colour encodes a real fact (§INV_PROVE_FAITHFUL_PRESENTATION).
- **composes** — eyebrow **R3** (naming the gate) → stamp **R1** → demoted title **R2** → ruling line **R2** (one sentence, naming the threshold) → gate stats **R4** → legend **R4** → apparatus **R4**. A `NOT_READY` / contested verdict is legal and should be stamped as such rather than rounded to pass or fail.
- **excludes** — **A giant-number hero** — two R1s (fight F1). **A verdict chip in the eyebrow** — the stamp already said the word. **Colour without the legend**, or colour as the only channel: each stamp here carries a distinct hand-drawn mark. **More than three stamps in a row** — past three it is a results table, and a table is a better table than a hero.
- **degrades to** — Threshold known but not yet resolved → **OP-H5 quiet** with a `status` chip at R3, honestly reading *pending*. No threshold at all → **OP-H3 thesis**: state the claim as a claim. Contested evidence (this session's 4.39:1 vs 4.74 contrast readings) → **thesis with both readings named** — never a stamp, because a stamp asserts closure the evidence does not have.
- *copyable markup:* `KIT_DIGEST_MARKUP.md` → "OP-H2 · verdict hero"

### OP-H3 · thesis / pull-quote opener
- **requires** — The finding is a **sentence**, not a number — one claim, **two lines or fewer** at display size, containing exactly one load-bearing phrase that can carry the emphasis (`LINE_ENTITY_DESIGN` §3: *a quoted line → quote / pull-quote*). It also requires an **as-of date**: a claim with no date is unfalsifiable, and an unfalsifiable claim set at 29px is just a poster.
- **composes** — label **R3** + verdict chip **R3** → claim **R1** → apparatus **R4**. The claim **replaces the title** — there is no separate title. A lede may follow at R2 if it starts the argument rather than restating the claim. When the line is genuinely quoted from a source, attribution is mandatory or the page adopts someone else's sentence as its own voice.
- **excludes** — **A separate title** — the reader would read the finding twice. **A dek** — a summary of a summary. **A stat strip above the claim** — numbers placed before a claim make the claim read as their caption, inverting the rank. **An accent-tinted panel behind the claim**: the left rule is the whole emphasis; a wash is depth spent on prose.
- **degrades to** — Claim runs past two display lines → **OP-H5 quiet** (title + dek): a claim you cannot set large is a claim you should set small. Claim is contested rather than settled → keep the form, drop the verdict chip, and **name both readings inside the claim** — the honest version of this hero is the one that says which part is not established.
- *copyable markup:* `KIT_DIGEST_MARKUP.md` → "OP-H3 · thesis / pull-quote opener"

### OP-H4 · split hero
- **requires** — A statement **and exactly one real visual** — either an exhibit whose path resolves, or a hand-authored SVG **whose every number also appears as text on the page** (the chart above prints 168 / 2 / 1 / 0). **Measured caveat**: `LINE_ENTITY_DESIGN` §2b found **zero image files anywhere in the corpus**, so in this system the image branch of this requirement is unmet by default and the degradation below is the normal case, not the exception.
- **composes** — Left: eyebrow **R3** → title **R1** → lede **R2**. Right: **exactly one** of {sparkline · single figure · dot cluster}, under a mono label. Apparatus **R4** spans both columns beneath. Below 760px the columns stack and the visual takes a hairline rule above it.
- **excludes** — **Two or three right-hand blocks stacked.** The catalog specimen shows three because it is a catalog; on a real page they compete for the same glance and the eye ping-pongs. **A placeholder or mocked asset** — a split hero built on a fake visual is the one opener that actively lies. **A visual whose values appear nowhere as text**: if a bar and a number can disagree, print the number.
- **degrades to** — **OP-H5 quiet**, with the visual moved down to the first content block where it can carry its own caption, legend and provenance. This is the normal outcome here. At ≤430px it degrades **automatically** — a stacked split is just a quiet opener with an orphan graphic, so prefer the explicit narrow composition in §7.
- *copyable markup:* `KIT_DIGEST_MARKUP.md` → "OP-H4 · split hero"

### OP-H5 · quiet hero — no hero at all
- **requires** — **Nothing.** This is the only opener with no precondition — which is precisely why it is the default and why the selection ladder in §6 terminates here. If you cannot state what a louder hero *requires*, you are looking at this one.
- **composes** — eyebrow **R3** → title **R1** → dek **or** subtitle **R2** → apparatus **R4** → lede. Everything in the parts inventory that is R3 or R4 attaches freely. A scope line may follow the lede.
- **excludes** — A figure, a stamp, a split — by definition; taking any of them means you are in H1/H2/H4 and owe that form's precondition. Otherwise **nothing is excluded**, and that is the point.
- **degrades to** — — *It is the floor.* There is nothing below it, which is what makes every other brief's **Degrades to** terminate.
- *copyable markup:* `KIT_DIGEST_MARKUP.md` → "OP-H5 · quiet hero — no hero at all"

## Creative-layout captions — 12 of 25

`CREATIVE_LAYOUTS.html` carries no four-clause contract; `preconditions.html` above contracts
the same catalogue. What is here and nowhere else is the **Remix** field — how to adapt.

- **01.1 Giant-number hero** — *Pattern:* **Giant-number hero** — the ONE number that *is* the finding, set huge in serif, with a one-line meaning + a supporting micro-stat row. *When:* The finding collapses to a single headline figure — a pass count, a dollar total, a percentage. Lead with the number, not the prose. *Remix:* Swap `.num` + `.unit` for your figure; recolor `.num` to `--defect` if the number is bad news; keep the micro row to 2–4 supporting stats or drop it entirely.
- **01.2 Thesis pull-quote opener** — *Pattern:* **Thesis pull-quote opener** — the finding stated as a large serif claim (drop-cap), with a verdict chip and a dated as-of line. *When:* The finding is a sentence, not a number — a claim you want the reader to accept at a glance before scrolling into the evidence. *Remix:* Rewrite the `.claim` sentence; italicize the load-bearing phrase with `<em>`; swap the chip to `CONFIRMED` / `REFUTED`; keep the as-of line honest — it dates the claim.
- **01.3 Verdict hero card** — *Pattern:* **Verdict hero card** — a bold PASS / FAIL / PROVEN card carrying the key metric + a one-line ruling; color encodes the real verdict. *When:* A gate, check, or claim resolves to a categorical verdict. Use one card for a single verdict, or a row to compare several gates side by side. *Remix:* Set the `.vcard` class to `pass`/`fail`/`proven`; swap the `.n` metric + `.ruling`; the legend below is mandatory whenever color carries meaning (`§INV_PROVE_FAITHFUL_PRESENTATION`).
- **01.4 Split hero** — *Pattern:* **Split hero** — claim/thesis in the left column, a key visual docked right (inline-SVG spark, a stat, or a freshness-dot cluster); the magazine "opener spread" feel. *When:* The finding pairs a statement with one supporting visual — a trend, a distribution, a headline stat. Best when the visual earns its place beside the words. *Remix:* Keep the left `.claim`; drop ANY one of the three right-hand blocks (spark / bignum / dot-cluster) — they're independent. Hand-author the SVG with `currentColor` + tokens; never a chart lib.
- **02.1 Diagonal split before / after** — Pattern Diagonal split  Use when one exhibit reads as a single object that changed — a rendered overlay, a screenshot, a scorecard — and you want the eye to cross a seam rather than compare two boxes.  **Remix:** two absolutely-positioned `.side` layers, each `clip-path`'d to complementary polygons; drop a `.deltabadge` at the seam with the headline number.
- **02.2 Overlay diff — was X, now Y** — Pattern Overlay diff  Use when the change is a small, precise edit to code, config, or a data value — the reader should see the old token struck through and the new token lit up in place, so the exact delta is unmissable.  **Remix:** wrap the removed token in `.was` (strike-through, defect hue) and the replacement in `.now` (highlight, fixed hue); lift the change into a serif `.quotable` line for the headline.
- **02.3 Side-by-side columns with a delta gutter** — Pattern Delta gutter  Use when you have several metrics that each moved — a benchmark table, a cost sheet — and the story is the *per-row* direction and size of change, not one headline number.  **Remix:** a 3-column grid (before · gutter · after); tag each gutter cell `.better` or `.worse` to color the ↑/↓ and Δ by whether the move is an improvement.
- **02.4 "Was → Now" transformation strip** — Pattern Was → Now strip  Use when you need a compact, single-line headline before/after near the top of a page — state A, a transform marker, state B — that a reader grasps in one glance without reading a table.  **Remix:** a 3-column strip (A · transform · B); label the transform with a mono pill for the mechanism and an inline SVG arrow; stacks vertically with a rotated arrow on narrow screens.
- **06.1 The claim-ledger, as a designed object** — Pattern **Claim-Ledger.** Each row is one claim: its evidence, a verdict chip, and a provenance tag. A double-ruled cap and foot frame it as a bound register, not a spreadsheet. **When to use:** a resolved investigation with 3–8 discrete claims you can each attach a verdict to. **How to remix:** swap the verdict vocabulary (`Proven / Partial / Refuted`) for your domain; the provenance tag column is fixed — every row must declare one.
- **06.2 Layered evidence-stack — one claim, many sources** — Pattern **Evidence-Stack.** A claim sits above a stack of overlapping source cards — a doc, a log line, a query result — so the reader sees the claim is backed by **multiple independent sources**, not one. The offset + shadow convey depth. **When to use:** a load-bearing claim you want to show is over-determined (converging evidence). **How to remix:** keep 2–4 cards per stack; each card names its source *kind* and provenance; the convergence line at the foot states what all sources agree on.
- **06.3 The receipt — audit trail as artifact** — Pattern **Receipt / Manifest.** A `--mono` itemized receipt of what was checked, with counts, a provenance column, a checksum, and a verdict footer. It reads as a printed audit trail. **When to use:** a verification pass with many small line-items (tests, greps, files) where the *completeness* of checking is the point. **How to remix:** each line carries a status glyph + a `here`/`up` tag; the checksum is a real digest of the inputs, and the total tallies the columns above it — keep them honest.
- **06.4 Trusted-vs-checked provenance ribbon** — Pattern **Provenance Ribbon.** A compact two-state visual language: a coloured left spine marks each assertion's provenance so the reader always knows, at a glance, what rests on the upstream finding versus what was verified here. **When to use:** flowing prose or a mixed narrative where claims of both kinds interleave. **How to remix:** the ribbon is the whole vocabulary — solid accent spine = `checked-here`, hatched spine = `trusted-upstream`. Keep the legend adjacent; never introduce a third state without adding it to the legend.

**No caption in the gallery (13)** — these patterns ship with no when/remix
guidance at all; their only contract is the sheet above.

## Static blocks — 20, use-when only

`PROOF_BLOCKS.html` carries no four-clause contract either. Its unique field is the
modifier vocabulary on each block.

- **stat-strip** `--tiled` — **Use when** the page opens on 3–5 headline figures of equal weight — the masthead ledger. `--tiled` gives each cell a state dot + footnote (the old KPI grid).
- **bignum** `--spark` — **Use when** one figure *is* the finding — label, movement, and an optional hand-drawn sparkline (the old metric-with-trend).
- **table** `--delta · --status · --total` — **Use when** the evidence is a run of cases. `--delta` colors a signed direction column; `--status` adds a pass/warn/fail pill; `--total` a summary row. Scrolls in-container.
- **meter** `SVG bars` — **Use when** figures are shares of a whole and their *relative* size is the point — hand-drawn bars, value labeled in text too.
- **sequence** `--timeline · --numbered · --log` — **Use when** order carries meaning, read top-to-bottom. `--timeline` = dated events with node states; `--numbered` = reproduction steps; `--log` = typed add/fix/chg stream.
- **pipeline** `--flow · --phases` — **Use when** a process moves left-to-right through named stages. `--flow` = arrow connectors; `--phases` = a state per stage (done / current / upcoming). Scrolls in-container.
- **branch** `decision fork` — **Use when** the logic forks on a condition and *both arms matter* — distinct from a linear sequence: it is a decision, not a progression.
- **claim-verdict** `claim → proof → verdict` — **Use when** each assertion should show its evidence and its ruling in one row — the spine of an evidence ledger.
- **thesis** `framing premise` — **Use when** one idea frames everything below it — the sentence you want the reviewer to leave with. Larger and quieter than a callout.
- **scope** `shown / out / upstream` — **Use when** honesty demands drawing the boundary — what's shown, what's out of scope, what rests on an upstream verdict.
- **qa** `verdict-led answers` — **Use when** you can anticipate the reviewer's questions — lead each answer with a one-word verdict they can scan.
- **tradeoff** `pros / cons` — **Use when** a decision has real costs on both sides — two columns, signed markers, no false balance.
- **figure** `plate frame` — **Use when** a real rendered asset is the evidence — the hatched placeholder stands in until the real capture drops in, never a mock passed off as real.
- **diff** `before / after` — **Use when** the fix is a small, quotable source delta — red pane is the literal pre-fix line, green pane the current source.
- **code** `--term` — **Use when** a quoted source excerpt is the proof. `--term` flips to dark terminal chrome for verbatim CLI output. Scrolls in-container; cited by file & line.
- **quote** `--pull` — **Use when** you lift a verbatim line and must attribute it — a provenance chip says whether it was checked here. `--pull` sets it large to interrupt the flow (the old pull-quote).
- **callout** `--insight · --caution · --note` — **Use when** a point needs to step out of the body with a stated intent — three tones, each with its own semantic hue and label. Absorbs the margin-note aside.
- **legend** `--freshness · --chips` — **Use when** any color on the page encodes a fact — the mandatory key that decodes it, and travels with it. `--freshness` = the recency scale; `--chips` = provenance / verdict.
- **verdict-dashboard** — **Use when** a page carries many claims and the reviewer wants *the whole ledger's state in one scan* — a severity stripe per cell.
- **coverage-map** — **Use when** you want the reviewer to see *what was checked vs. deliberately skipped*, spatially — solid = verified, dashed = out-of-scope by choice, red = a named gap.
